title: 第7章 夜问第8章 梦中魇
content_zh:
夜渐深了，杜若院里的灯还亮着。
宝儿端着一盆热水进来，放在榻边的脚凳上，拧了帕子递给杜若。
杜若接过去敷在脸上，热汽氤氲，模糊了她的眉眼。
宝儿便蹲下身去替她脱鞋，动作熟稔又自然，像是在杜家做了许多年的丫鬟。
门外传来值夜婆子的一声哈欠，随后是脚步拖沓着远去的声响。宝儿站起身，走到门边，探头往外看了一眼——廊下空空荡荡，只有灯笼在风里轻轻摇晃。
她掩上门，插上门闩。
再转过身时，她的眼神变了，像两盏被点燃的灯，光芒内敛而深邃。
她的脊背也挺直了——周身透出一股子清冷的气息，像是山巅终年不化的积雪。
杜若靠在榻上，看着她，嘴角微微扬起。
“上仙这模样，倒是比方才顺眼多了。”
君澜——此刻恢复了本来面目的女仙——在绣墩上坐下，也不端架子，只是淡淡地看了杜若一眼。
“你倒是适应得快。”君澜道。
“不适应又能怎样？”杜若抬起手，在烛火下翻来覆去地看着这双陌生的手，腕上那只碧玉镯子在火光中泛着温润的光，“这具身体已经给了我，我总不能天天哭哭啼啼地说‘我不要’吧？”
君澜没有接话。
杜若放下手，目光落在窗纸上。窗外夜色沉沉，偶尔传来一两声秋虫的鸣叫，断断续续的，像是气力不足。
“上仙，”杜若道，“那个真正的杜若……她的魂魄，您渡走了吗？”
“渡了。”
“她去哪儿了？”
君澜沉默了一瞬，才道：“去该去的地方。”
杜若听出这句话里的回避之意，便没有再追问。

她虽然附身才一日，却已经隐约明白了一个道理——在这世间，有些事是活人不能问的，问了也没有答案。
“这具身体，我可以用多久？”她想了想，换了个话题。
君澜愣了一下，随即笑了。那笑容很淡，像水面上一圈即将消散的涟漪。
“肉身凡胎，自然有朽坏的一天。”
君澜的语气依旧平淡，“但你的灵识附在其中，只要不遭横祸，活上几十年是不成问题的。”
“几十年呀，”杜若的目光担忧起来，“不知道我那树身可否撑几十年，我是茶灵，附身于人体，总归不是办法。”
君澜看着她，目光里多了一丝说不清道不明的东西。
屋里安静了一会儿，烛花啪地炸开，落下一小截灰烬。
杜若重新靠回榻上，忽然问道：“上仙，您在杜家看出什么来了没有？”
“你指什么？”
“那个杜茂源。”杜若的目光微微眯起来，像一只在暗处观察猎物的猫，“他是真的疼女儿吗？”
君澜没有立刻回答。她伸手拿起桌上的茶壶，给自己倒了一杯水。水是凉的，她也不在意，端起来抿了一口，放下。
content_en:
The night is getting darker, and the lights in Du Ruo's courtyard are still on.
Bao'er came in with a basin of hot water, placed it on the footstool next to the couch, twisted the handkerchief and handed it to Du Ruo.
Du Ruo took it and applied it on her face. The hot steam blurred her eyebrows.
Bao'er knelt down and took off her shoes, his movements familiar and natural, as if he had been a maid in the Du family for many years.
There was a yawn from the night lady outside the door, followed by the sound of footsteps shuffling away. Bao'er stood up, walked to the door, and looked out - the corridor was empty, except for the lantern swaying gently in the wind.
She closed the door and bolted it.
When she turned around again, her eyes changed, like two lit lamps, the light was restrained and deep.
Her back also straightened - there was a cold aura around her, like the snow on the top of the mountain that never melts all year round.
Du Ruo leaned on the couch, looked at her, and raised the corners of his mouth slightly.
"Shangxian's appearance is much more pleasing to the eye than before."
Jun Lan—the fairy who had returned to her true self at this moment—sat down on the embroidered pier without showing any airs, and just glanced at Du Ruo lightly.
"You adapt quickly." Jun Lan said.
"So what if I don't adapt?" Du Ruo raised his hand and looked at the unfamiliar hands over and over under the candlelight. The jasper bracelet on his wrist glowed warmly in the firelight. "This body has been given to me. I can't cry and say 'I don't want it' every day, right?"
Jun Lan didn't answer.
Du Ruo put down his hand and looked at the window paper. It was dark outside the window, and occasionally one or two chirps of autumn insects could be heard, intermittent, as if due to lack of energy.
"Shangxian," Du Ruo said, "The real Du Ruo...have you passed away her soul?"
"Crossed."
"Where did she go?"
Jun Lan was silent for a moment and then said: "Go where you should go."
Du Ruo heard the avoidance in this sentence and did not ask any more questions.
Although she has only been possessed for a day, she has already vaguely understood a truth - in this world, there are some things that a living person cannot ask, and even if she asks, there will be no answer.
"How long can I use this body?" She thought for a moment and changed the subject.
Jun Lan was stunned for a moment, then smiled. The smile was very faint, like a ripple on the water that was about to dissipate.
"The mortal body will naturally decay one day."
Jun Lan's tone was still calm, "But with your spiritual consciousness attached to it, as long as you don't suffer any misfortune, it won't be a problem to live for decades."
"Decades," Du Ruo's eyes became worried, "I don't know if my tree body can last for decades. I am a tea spirit. Possessing the human body is not an option."
Jun Lan looked at her, with something inexplicable in his eyes.
The room was quiet for a while, then the candle exploded and a small amount of ashes fell.
Du Ruo leaned back on the couch and suddenly asked: "Shangxian, did you see anything in the Du family?"
"What do you mean?"
"That Du Maoyuan." Du Ruo's eyes narrowed slightly, like a cat observing its prey in the dark, "Does he really love his daughter?"
Jun Lan did not answer immediately. She reached for the teapot on the table and poured herself a glass of water. The water was cold, but she didn't care. She picked it up, took a sip, and put it down.
